name: Value-based Business Strategy & Innovation
description: The central question of the course is, how do firms capture value from innovation and from other activities? The business world is full of examples of firms that created considerable value, through innovation or otherwise, but had to give up most of that value to competitors, complementors, customers, or other parties. We tackle this question from various directions. Qualitative approaches such as the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Teece’s Profiting-From-Innovation (PFI) framework provide a conceptual understanding. Game-theoretic approaches, using both non-cooperative and cooperative game theory, provide an analytical understanding of the drivers of value capture. Emphasis will be on mathematical models from Value Capture Theory, a stream of research recently reviewed by Gans and Ryall (2017) and initiated by Brandenburger and Stuart’s (1996) study of Value-based Business Strategy. We will test predictions of Value Capture Theory through negotiation experiments in class.
prerequisites: Good mathematical skills corresponding to a Bachelor’s course in mathematics (e.g., calculating derivatives, solving systems of equations, doing integrations), and an interest in translating real-world problems into formal representations. Recommended: Bachelor-level knowledge of strategy and of technology and innovation management.
